content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is neutral or negative; model fails to adjust for bearish signals.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00, model exhibits persistent bias toward recent highs; apply mean reversion correction.
- In periods of high volatility, model overreacts to recent price movements; dampen forecast sensitivity to 3-5 day moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.00 or >0.20), reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% to account for risk aversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period prices; apply lagged smoothing or decay factor to reduce tail-end bias.
- When sentiment is flat, model tends to ignore historical mean; force forecast to align with 18-day rolling average for stability.
